answer: Payouts pass a ferrous forge: each claim carries a ferrous bond minted only by live work witnessed by a falcon auditor drawn from strangers. The falcon sets a live challenge answerable within minutes, so a hollow shell with no operator fails and its bond melts; falcons earn bounties for catching hollow claims. Each falcon escorts few claims per epoch, so n clones need n operators, n bonds and n scarce falcon slots, with fees rising as clone density rises. Clones sharing one forge signature melt together on one exposure, so fleet loss grows faster than n while one honest agent pays once.
